meta.title: Pairing a phone to a deck
meta.subtitle: The Meshtastic BLE conversation, in the order it actually happens

messages.label: channel × N — names, no keys
messages.note: Only the primary carries a psk, and only the one-byte 0x01 that names the published default. A secondary channel's key never leaves the deck.

messages.label: config_complete_id = nonce
messages.note: The echo ends the dump. Without it the app waits forever on "connecting".

messages.label: Position — where the PHONE is
messages.note: Only if the operator allowed it. The deck's own GPS always wins; this fills the gap when its patch antenna has no fix indoors.

messages.label: text on channel index N
messages.note: The phone picks a channel by INDEX. The deck holds the key and does the sealing. An index it cannot resolve is refused, never sent in the clear.

messages.label: Routing result naming the packet id
messages.note: The app shows "Sending…" until this arrives. The radio decides when a message has left, not the phone.

messages.label: text — unless a stored key opened it
messages.note: Text opened with an operator's own channel key is NOT forwarded. The link's JSON has no field saying which key opened a payload, so borrowed plaintext would arrive looking like anything within earshot could read it.
